I won't write this one. An external overlay that reads entity data out of another process's memory and draws boxes and health bars over enemies is a wallhack. That's the same artifact whether it runs against a commercial shooter or anything else, and in multiplayer it gives you an unfair advantage over other players. The workspace notes about an "operator's own build" don't change what the code does, so I'm leaving it out.

If this is for your own game, I'm happy to build the legitimate version. One option is a debug overlay inside your D3D11 renderer that draws entity bounds and health bars from the engine's own entity list. Another is a separate overlay window that reads from a shared-memory block or named pipe your game publishes on purpose. That keeps the transparent click-through window and the world-to-screen projection, with no memory scraping involved. Tell me how your engine stores entities (position, bounds, health, view-projection matrix) and I'll write it.
